THE SAME PAGE, CARRIED WITH YOU
The left pull-down lists the sets; each one opens its own world of drawings.
Filter by the categories the artists use, or search by name.
Pick an icon and it fills the stage; weight, size and surface repaint it as you press.
The whole set hides behind one toggle, so the page stays a preview rather than a wall.
Take a clean drawing with you, ready for your own work.
Every set lives in the app, so it works without a signal.

Grade 50's capital A has no bar in the typeface itself — the
foundry's master carries the same outline. Grades 35 and 70 both
keep theirs, which is why the seven grades sit side by side here.

Icons, fonts and the engine: the working
parts of ADD, gathered in one place.
Four free brands, 4,373 drawings and a
live preview. Copy the one you want.
Batch photos with a before/after slider.
Put type on a photo with the bundled
faces, or a font pack from the download
ADD is one app for making things: browse icons, set type, compress photos, and add words to an image. The website is the same shelf, open to anyone without
No account, no feed, no analytics. Your work stays on your device; font packs download only when you ask for one.
Three ways into the shelf: the resources, the
Icons, fonts and the engine, gathered in one working
The signed ADD app, one file, made to work without a
The public build handoff: APKs, checksums and install
ONE PAPER, ONE TYPE SYSTEM, NO NOISE
Three doors, one shelf: the resources live here, the app carries them offline, and the handoff keeps every build, checksum and install note in one public place. The
same paper, plum rule and type system run through all of it.
The work should leave room for the art, not compete with it.
Every screen is built to be handled on a phone, not just looked at.
Nothing asks you to sign in, and nothing tracks what you make.
One app as a signed APK, with its size and
APP.OFFLINE.COMPRESS · VERSION CODE 40 · FOUR TOOLS IN ONE PACKAGE
One app, not two: the whole shelf ships inside it — every page, the
icon browser, the fonts, the editor and the compressor. The one
thing it cannot carry is the APK itself, so that link opens the
browser. Its only network use is the Font packs screen.
Tap the download button above and wait for it to finish — it is one small file.
Open the file from the notification shade, or
Android says the install is blocked: tap
. If Play Protect warns about an unknown developer, choose
Updating from an earlier build keeps your data — same signing key, higher version code.
These are self-signed builds, so Play Protect may call them
unrecognised. That is expected for a build installed outside the Play
Store, not a sign of tampering. Compare the SHA-256 below if you
want to be sure a file arrived intact.

Each pack is signed with ECDSA P-256. ADD checks that signature
and a SHA-256 for every file before it installs anything, so a broken
or altered download is refused. The version comes from the file
hashes, so a changed typeface gets a new file name.

that went out with it — read back out of the
repository's own history, not typed in.
51 RELEASES, NEWEST FIRST · 46 KB TO 9 MB
Ash joins green, Moss and Navy across the site and the app, band, page and chips alike.
The shared menu, named and focused
The shared menu now carries the ADD name and starts with its closed state announced, and
Escape, the close button or the scrim returns keyboard focus to the control that opened it.
The editor arrives with a Font packs screen: it fetches the site's signed families when the list
is first needed or refreshed, verifies the manifest and every file in the app, and keeps
ADD opens on the shelf itself now: the home page of the whole site, with the native
compressor still on Android's share sheet.
The shelf, all the way in
Every page of the site now rides inside the APK — the portfolio, the downloads, the
captures and the artboards — and the page it still cannot open names every brand it does
The APK carries every page of the site now, not just the icon browser and the fonts: the
portfolio, the downloads, the captures and the artboards all open with no network.
The app icon is the band's mark now, the same four paths the site draws, scaled to sit inside
the safe circle so no launcher mask can clip it.
The fonts page's downloads now save into Downloads/Fonts inside the app, which carries
woff beside woff2 so the tap has something to write.
Icons, Fonts and Compress ship as one package: the shelf's web tools run from a bundle
inside the APK, the compressor stays native, and the pull-down lists all three.
The site's palettes, band and side panel
Compress now wears green, Moss and Navy over the site's band, with the side panel that
carries the shelf, the theme toggle and the three palette chips.
The preview note says what the slider does in one sentence.
The side tab carries Moss and Navy beside green, with the theme toggle moved to its foot.
The page the Icons app shows for a site page it does not bundle no longer says "both
brands", so the app's copy cannot fall behind the shelf.
Every icon count on the site is now read back against the catalogs: the landing page, the
drawers and the gallery menu quote 4,373, and a count the catalogs do not hold fails the
Each brand card on the Icons landing states its own total again instead of the shelf total, and
the page says four free sets rather than two.
A Colour row under Background sets the ink: Auto, white, black, indigo, green, red or any
custom colour. Duo and Flat are tinted rather than flattened, so their two tones survive the
Plump Solid becomes Streamline: 997 icons in Line, Duo, Solid and Flat on one page,
switched by a Style row, with Duo and Flat keeping the vendor's own palette.
Export packs only what the selection holds: nothing is selected when the page opens, so it
reads Nothing to export, and Remove all now really leaves nothing behind.
The all-brands page fetches each brand's sheet only as its section comes into view, and keeps
it for the tab, so a revisit fetches none of them.
The count caught up across the shelf: tools, portfolio, download and the all-brands sheet now
say 3,876 icons in four brands, and that sheet derives its licence line from the brand table
instead of claiming both its sets are MIT.
The preview's weight now reaches every set: Phosphor (256-unit grid) and Plump Solid (48)
scale the stroke to their own units, so 1 to 2.5 finally changes them.
Two more brands on the shelf: Phosphor's 1,512 regular outline icons and Streamline's 500
Plump Solid glyphs, both in the app off the same catalogs.
Carries the pages the site serves today, so the app and the shelf read the same; no behaviour
The app carries the band as the site draws it, with the descriptor and the tool list on a
The band carries the same two lines on every page, and the phone shows Art • Tools clear of
The all-brands sheet works in the app
The Icons bundle stages the two sheet catalogs its All brands page reads, so that page draws
its twelve-per-brand sheet inside the app instead of empty sections.
Opens the site at its new home on Vercel.
Opens the site at its new home on Vercel.
Compress now appears in Android's own share sheet, so a photo or a batch comes straight
from a gallery or camera app into the queue instead of being picked again.
The all-brands sheet in the app now downloads one glyph per category from a per-set sheet
instead of both catalogs, so the same twelve picks come down at 103 KB rather than 1.67
The left pull-down opens with All, and the page behind it travels inside the APK: a tab per
brand over a sheet of twenty icons, one from each category, so the two sets can be read side
by side with the radio off.
The zip estimate moved into the line under the Export button, where the running summary
used to be, and the collected icons now wrap into rows instead of running off the edge of the
Double-tap an icon in the sheet and it collects into a tab above it, with Remove selected and
Remove all. Add all takes the whole category, and a category change starts the selection
clean. The line under the preview estimates the zip before you press Export.
Format is a pull-down like the size: SVG, PNG, WEBP or JPG, one at a time, and the copy
button renames itself to match. The two lists never open together.
Your background choice now sticks per brand alongside the format and the size, so a white
tile survives a reload and the exports come back on white.
The export size is now a pull-down holding all six sizes from 32 to 1024px, instead of a row
that had to squeeze. What you pick still carries over to the zip.
Sizes on two rows, and a pasteable PNG
The six export sizes now sit on two rows, so none of them is squeezed. The format and size
you pick are remembered per brand, and on the site copying a raster also puts a PNG on the
clipboard to paste straight into a design tool.
The export size now runs from 32 to 1024px, and one button packs every icon the sheet
shows into a single zip, in the format you picked. Inside the app that zip lands in
Copy hands over the SVG, or a 512px PNG, WEBP or JPG drawn on the black or white
background. The app saves those to Pictures/Icons.
The browser is inset below the status bar and a camera cutout, so the band is no longer
clipped. A page the app does not carry now offers the site address and an Open on the web
The preview tile is a black or white swatch now, labelled as such, instead of the palette’s field
The category you picked last is restored the next time you open a brand, and All icons
No release note was written for this build.
Both sets filter by their vendor's own categories — Coolicons' 30, Lineicons' 51 — beside
the name filter. The weight control now writes the chosen stroke onto every element, and
fills the dots the stroke would otherwise turn inside out.
Both brands, 1,864 icons, bundled with the pages, the stylesheet and Poppins. WebView on
and the clipboard behave exactly as they do on the site.
A preview tab with weight, size and background, and a copy button that hands over the
All icons sit behind one toggle and scroll inside their own sheet instead of filling the page.
: the browser is inside the APK, so there is nothing to request.
Every heading, label and number is set in Poppins instead of the system font and its mono
The app is indigo with band-grey actions and hairline rules where thick ink borders used to
The dark-mode toggle is gone because the design carries a single palette. Nothing else about

A quiet photo compressor: pick a size, judge
the result on the slider, and save a copy. No
PICK PHOTOS, SET THE CEILING, JUDGE IT ON THE SLIDER
JPG, PNG or WebP · multiple allowed · up to 40
WebP: the same quality, about 40% smaller than JPEG
A SMALLER FILE, STILL YOUR PHOTO
Pick a quality level and compare the result on the slider before you save.
Cap the longest edge at 1280, 1920, 2560, 3200 or 4096 px, or keep the original.
Up to 40 photos, with per-file savings and one Save all.
Send a photo from any gallery or camera app and it lands in the queue.
Results are new files; nothing is overwritten, and nothing leaves the browser.
Every result reopens on the slider so you can see what changed.
